title: Adaptive activation-scale transfer pipeline (SmoothQuant-compatible) and microkernel runtime support
creator: Ava Kim
description: Implement an adaptive activation-scale transfer pipeline that produces SmoothQuant-compatible INT8 profiles and integrates a small set of specialized microkernels into the runtime. The goal is to enable per-layer activation rebalancing (scale transfer) during offline calibration and to expose runtime hooks that select the microkernel variant when a profile includes activation-transfer metadata. Work includes: a calibration replay harness that records layer-wise scale ratios, a profile format extension (backwards-compatible) to store transfer hints, an offline optimizer that folds transfer into weight scales where possible, and runtime changes to dispatch microkernels and fall back to generic kernels when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces profile JSON with activation_transfer entries for >=95% of layers for transformer-encoder workloads
INT8 inference with activation-transfer microkernels matches FP16/FP32 token-level perplexity to within 1.5% on validation prompt sets
Runtime selects microkernel when profile indicates transfer, and falls back without correctness loss when microkernel not available
End-to-end CI includes a lightweight accuracy regression test and perf benchmark showing <=10% latency increase vs baseline INT8 for short-context generation (<=256 tokens)
tasks: Design profile extension: add activation_transfer {scale_source, scale_target, strength} metadata
Implement calibration replay harness (record per-layer activations and compute transfer ratios)
Build offline optimizer to apply foldable transfers into weights and mark non-foldable transfers for runtime handling
Implement two microkernel variants: transfer-aware matmul and transfer-aware fused-linear-gelu (AVX/SM80 prototypes)
Runtime dispatch: load profile, validate kernel compatibility, select microkernel or generic path
Add unit/integration tests and accuracy regression harness, add perf microbenchmarks
Create docs for profile format and developer guide for microkernel contributions
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Profile extension chosen as small JSON delta to avoid changing storage/replication: keeps backward compatibility (runtime treats unknown fields as no-op)
Two-phase approach: foldable transfers at build time to avoid runtime overhead; only remaining non-foldable transfers handled by microkernels
Microkernels target common hardware families first (x86 AVX512 + NVIDIA SM80) to reduce engineering scope; fallback ensures functionality elsewhere
Calibration replay is deterministic but adds runtime memory footprint during calibration; we limit replay window by sampling activations per-layer to bound memory
implementation_notes: Calibration replay reuses existing eval harness with a new 'activation_probe' interface to capture max/quantile statistics
Optimizer uses a conservative foldability analysis: can fold if transfer ratio < 1.1 and weight-per-channel quantization invariant holds
Microkernels accept optional per-input scale vectors (for activation-transfer compensation) and expose an ISA-level fast-path when strength == 1.0
Runtime checks profile schema version; if version > 1 it logs a detectable metric but continues with best-effort compatibility
test_plan: Unit tests for profile parser and foldability analyzer
Calibration CI job: run harness on small BERT and Llama-7B subsets and compare accuracy to FP16 baseline
Performance microbenchmarks across common sequence lengths (8, 64, 256) and batch sizes (1, 8, 16)
Canary rollout in dedicated infra pool with traffic shadowing for two weeks before broader rollout
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Microkernels could introduce subtle numeric divergence. Mitigation: staged rollout, rigorous token-level regression tests, and ability to force-disable microkernels per-customer
Risk: Calibration replay could be slow for long sequences. Mitigation: activation sampling and parallelized replay across calibration shards
Risk: Profile incompatibility with older runtime. Mitigation: runtime ignores unknown transfer fields and adds metrics to detect usage
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind runtime feature flag
Enable offline optimizer in CI and generate sample profiles for validation
Deploy runtime change to staging and run shadowed traffic with microkernels enabled
If metrics stable for 48h, enable for 10% of dedicated fleet; monitor accuracy and latency; proceed to 100% over 7 days
